allJobs.description: About this Role St Thomas’ is a special place with a group of dedicated staff who are committed to ensuring that our children receive the very best education and where our children grow to be confident, highly motivated and happy. As a Church of England school, our school vision 'Growing, Learning and Shining Together with God' underpins all that we do. Core Purpose The core purpose of a Teaching Assistant at a Manor MAT School is to enhance children's learning. It is to work alongside the teacher in the classroom, in support of pupil’s learning, including those with Special Educational needs under the direction and guidance of the class teacher. It is to make a contribution to the planning of the learning, to help pupils to access the tasks expected of them, to support as appropriate and to help monitor their progress. It is important that teacher and teaching assistant work closely together in order to make the best use of the time available in the classroom. These principles apply whether or not the pupils have Special Educational Needs. Key Objectives To support and uphold the school’s vision and values. To help children of all abilities, including those with special educational needs to learn as effectively and independently as possible, both individually and in small groups. To run a range of interventions to support individuals and small groups. To prepare materials and resources to support individuals, small groups and classroom learning opportunities. To support children’s emotional development and resilience when approaching learning tasks. To support children’s behaviour in line with the school’s vision, values and positive behaviour policy. To have an awareness of and adherence to all school safeguarding procedures and participate in training as appropriate. To ensure the health and safety of the children and to report any concerns or details of accidents/incidents as necessary to the Headteacher. To implement and promote the schools equal opportunities policies at all times and to value diversity. To support the school’s wide range of extra - curricular activities; including helping to run a club. Employee Benefits A dedicated and friendly staff team who are committed to delivering the best education and services for children and staff within the Trust. CPD opportunities in-line with role The chance to join a growing Academy who are committed to raising standards and achieving excellence for all pupils VivUp - Employee Benefits scheme (https://vivupbenefits.co.uk/) Manor Multi Academy Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children. We will ensure that all our recruitment and selection practices reflect this vision. Successful candidates will be subject to an Enhanced DBS check along with other relevant employment checks. Manor Multi Academy Trust is an Equal Opportunities employer. This post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 and is eligible for an enhanced DBS check including a Children's Barring List Check. If you are barred from working with children, you are breaking the law if you apply for this post. Online Search An online search will be undertaken on all shortlisted candidates. This search does not form part of the shortlisting process, and you will have the opportunity to discuss any issues of concern that may arise from this search at the interview. Informal visits to school are welcome. To arrange a visit please contact the school office. Interview date to be confirmed.

allJobs.title: Teacher of Maths (maternity cover)
allJobs.location: New Milton, South East, United Kingdom
allJobs.description: We are seeking a passionate and dynamic Maths Teacher, to join our dedicated and innovative team at The Arnewood School. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the future success of our thriving Mathematics department and make a significant impact on students' outcomes and understanding of mathematics. You will play a crucial role within the Maths team in enhancing the teaching and learning experience for our students. You will work closely with staff and students, leading by example and helping to create a culture of excellence and high achievement in mathematics. In our department, teachers put a large emphasis on success through high-quality explanations, guided practice, independent practice and regular feedback. We have a detailed curriculum plan and students work to achieve a strong understanding of Mathematical concepts before moving on. For the successful candidate this is a unique opportunity to join a superb team and shape the department's future success. The Mathematics department has embarked on a journey to improve student outcomes through a focus on a mastery approach, whilst reducing workload at every opportunity. We do not expect books to be marked, but instead focus on timely and effective feedback. We want everyone to have the time and space to improve their skills, whether that is students or staff, and as a department, we will continue to invest in this. The successful candidate will have a strong and secure knowledge of the GCSE curriculum. They will have excellent leadership and communication skills, with the ability to inspire and motivate others. They will be able to maintain and build on a culture of success where all feel valued and proud of their achievements. They will be ably supported by motivated members of the Maths Team so that we can deliver excellent outcomes for all our students whatever their starting point. We are dedicated in ensuring all lessons are pitched appropriately, so that our students are able to thrive. We are committed to all students developing a love of mathematics and a desire to achieve the very best they can. The successful candidate will demonstrate: - A passion for mathematics and teaching and have excellent subject knowledge and pedagogical understanding They are an excellent classroom practitioner, who is experienced in teaching maths at key Stages 3 and 4. The ability to motivate, challenge, support and inspire students to achieve the best possible outcomes Outstanding success at achieving consistently good results in mathematics, at key stage 3 and key stage 4 The ability to create and facilitate highly challenging and engaging lessons They are optimistic, positive, cheerful and develop others to flourish. Excellent communication skills A commitment to ongoing professional development and staying current with educational best practices.

allJobs.title: Intervention Tutor
allJobs.description: Intervention Tutor St Nicholas Catholic Academy, Liverpool Could you be the person who changes the trajectory of a child's education? At St Nicholas Catholic Academy , part of St Joseph Catholic Multi Academy Trust , we believe every child deserves the opportunity to succeed, regardless of their starting point. Due to a significant increase in pupil numbers and the proven impact of our intervention model, we are seeking an exceptional Intervention Tutor to join our growing academy community on a permanent basis. This is an opportunity to play a pivotal role in transforming educational outcomes for children who need it most. A school that is growing and thriving St Nicholas is one of Liverpool's fastest-growing primary schools. Our pupil population has increased dramatically from 156 pupils to 194, with numbers expected to exceed 210 pupils , bringing new opportunities and new challenges. Many pupils join us throughout the academic year, often having experienced disruption to their education, gaps in learning, language barriers or significant challenges in accessing the curriculum. For these children, effective intervention is not an optional extra. It is life-changing. That's why this role is so important. Why this role exists The success of our intervention programme has been remarkable. Our targeted support has helped pupils make accelerated progress in reading, writing and mathematics, contributing to strong outcomes across the school, including impressive Key Stage 2 attainment and significant improvements for vulnerable learners and pupils with SEND. At a time when many schools are reducing support programmes, St Nicholas has taken the strategic decision to invest further because we know intervention works. We know that when children receive the right support at the right time, they flourish. The successful candidate will join a team committed to ensuring that no child falls behind because of circumstances beyond their control. The difference you'll make You'll work directly with children who need additional support in reading, phonics and mathematics, helping them develop the confidence, skills and knowledge needed to thrive in the classroom. You will: Deliver high-quality, structured interventions in reading and mathematics. Support children who are at risk of falling behind their peers. Work with pupils who have joined the school mid-year and need rapid support to access learning. Build confidence, resilience and positive attitudes towards education. Use assessment information to monitor progress and celebrate success. Work closely with teachers, leaders and support staff to ensure interventions have maximum impact. Contribute to whole-school literacy and numeracy improvement strategies. Every day you will see the direct impact of your work on children's lives. Who we're looking for We're seeking someone who: Is passionate about improving outcomes for children. Believes every child can achieve with the right support. Has strong literacy and numeracy skills. Can build positive and trusting relationships with pupils. Is organised, reflective and motivated by pupil progress. Works collaboratively with colleagues and families. Is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children. Shares and supports the Catholic ethos and values of the academy. Experience of phonics, reading interventions, tutoring, SEND support or primary education would be advantageous, but most importantly we are looking for someone who genuinely wants to make a difference. Why join St Nicholas Catholic Academy? This is an exciting time to join us. Our academy is growing rapidly and serves a wonderfully diverse community in the heart of Liverpool. We are proud of our inclusive ethos, ambitious culture and unwavering commitment to ensuring every child receives an excellent education. You'll be joining a dedicated team that: Places children at the centre of every decision. Invests in professional development and staff wellbeing. Celebrates collaboration and innovation. Values every member of staff. Understands the transformative power of education. At St Nicholas, you won't simply deliver interventions. You'll help children develop the skills, confidence and self-belief that will shape their futures. Come and see what makes St Nicholas special We know that choosing the right school is about more than reading a job description. We warmly encourage prospective applicants to visit the academy and experience first-hand the welcoming atmosphere, dedicated staff team and wonderful children that make St Nicholas Catholic Academy such a rewarding place to work. A visit will give you the opportunity to see our intervention provision in action, learn more about our vision for the future and meet the people who make our academy such a special place. To arrange a school tour or an informal conversation about the role, please contact Alison McLoughlin on 0151 709 5532 or email office@stnicholas.sjcmat.co.uk . Be part of something bigger At St Nicholas Catholic Academy, we know that targeted intervention changes lives. With increasing pupil numbers, significant levels of mobility and a growing demand for personalised support, this role has become a vital part of our long-term strategy for success. The successful candidate will help ensure that every child, regardless of their starting point, has the opportunity to learn, achieve and flourish. Join us and become part of a team that is making a measurable and lasting difference to children's lives every single day.

We are a popular employer to potential applicants and have a strong track record of attracting and retaining high-quality staff. We value and prioritise our staff and have a comprehensive programme of support, both in terms of professional development and personal support. All staff have access to our comprehensive EAP (Employee Assistance Programme) which includes benefits like free physiotherapy appointments, telephone GP access, counselling and financial advice to name a few. We have several staff social groups including an LGBTQ+ group, a theatre group, and staff yoga. We also have several staff social events each year. We are an open school and are always keen to work with other organisations and networks as we believe in community and sharing support and expertise. We are currently supporting another local secondary school through the RISE (DfE) programme and have strong working relationships with both of our local universities too. We are an ambitious school and are continually developing and improving our provision and approaches to ensure we can provide our children with the best education possible. By joining our School, we can offer you: Professional Development & Excellence An ethos of ‘High Achievement with Care and Discipline for All’ Excellent CPD Opportunities An Outstanding Ofsted Judgement A strong Progress 8 score Leading Edge Status Wellbeing & Support Mental health and wellbeing services such as access to a 24/7 confidential employee assistance programme Healthcare schemes such as Specsavers Eyecare vouchers for DSE users Cycle to Work Scheme Financial Benefits Incremental Pay Progression Generous Occupational Pension Scheme Blue Light Card The Fernwood School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff to share this commitment. allJobs.title: Pastoral Leader (Attendance)
allJobs.location: Witham, East of England, United Kingdom
allJobs.description: We're looking for a pastoral leader to join our school and help every student feel supported, safe and ready to thrive. This is a chance to make a real difference to young people's lives - removing barriers to attendance, building trusted relationships with families, and creating a culture where every child feels they belong. In this role, you'll work closely with students, staff, families and external agencies to promote positive attendance, support wellbeing, and help shape the caring, ambitious ethos we want for our school community. Key responsibilities You will: provide pastoral support to students, including those in at-risk groups, and act as a key contact when needed; work alongside the attendance officer to create and review attendance plans, follow up absences, and guide interventions that help improve punctuality and attendance; meet with families and external agencies to understand and address barriers to attendance, and support reintegration after any suspension; manage school attendance systems accurately, ensuring registers are completed on time and coding is clear and correct; collaborate with the safeguarding team, SENDCo and mental health lead to identify vulnerable students and coordinate support; and represent the school at inter-agency meetings and keep senior leaders informed of outcomes and actions. What we're looking for We're looking for someone who: holds GCSE maths and English (grade 4 or equivalent); brings experience of motivating young people and promoting high expectations; can use data thoughtfully to spot patterns, track progress and guide decisions; has strong interpersonal skills and can build relationships with students, families, staff and external agencies; stays calm under pressure, thinks creatively, and uses their own initiative within agreed ways of working; and shows patience, empathy and a non-judgemental approach, with a genuine passion for supporting every young person to succeed. Experience in an educational setting, knowledge of attendance legislation, and familiarity with Google Workspace would all be valuable. Could you be the person who helps our students feel valued, supported and ready to learn every day? About our school Lift Maltings is an 11-16 school based in Witham, Essex. Situated between the cities of Chelmsford and Colchester, the school has 900 students on roll and benefits from a modern, purpose-built site opened in 2011. With excellent transport links to London, our staff and students can take full advantage of the wealth of opportunities the capital provides. Free car parking facilities are available on site. Visits to the school are warmly encouraged. For an informal discussion about the post, please contact Luke Harper, School Operations Manager. Who is Lift Schools? Lift Schools is made up of 62 primary, secondary and special schools, educating more than 35,000 pupils across the country. We believe education can transform lives - and we want every child in our schools to achieve their full potential. How we support you We want you to feel supported, valued and able to grow throughout your career with Lift Schools. From high-quality professional development and career progression to wellbeing support and opportunities to connect and collaborate across our network, we invest in you so you can do your best work.

allJobs.title: Employer Partnerships Lead
allJobs.location: Hull, Yorkshire and the Humber, United Kingdom
allJobs.description: Ready to bring your expertise to a dynamic national network? We are looking for an immediate starter to join us on a fixed-term basis through 31 August 2027 (with potential to extend into 2028). Working 22.5 hours per week (preferably Tuesday through Thursday, with built-in flexibility), you'll enjoy a home-based setup with all travel expenses covered when visiting our schools and London office. Your new organisation Lift Schools are one of the largest multi-academy trusts in the country made up of 62 primary, secondary and special schools, educating more than 35,000 pupils. Our incredible Chief Executive, Rebecca (Becks) Boomer-Clark, joined in 2021 and has a clear objective, an excellent education for every child, in every classroom, every day regardless of background, geography or ability. We are thrilled to have secured funding from the DHL UK Foundation and to be working in partnership with them on their GoTeach initiative, which supports young people from underserved communities across the UK access decent employment and thrive in their careers. After a very successful first year of the programme, we are entering year 2 of a planned 3 year project. Impact and funding is reviewed by DHL UK Foundation at the end of each academic year. This role is advertised to the end of year 2 initially (31 Aug 2027) however, we expect to extend the role into year 3 of the project. We are now looking for a part-time Employee Partnership Lead to play an integral part in leading this exciting partnership as a maternity cover. Your new role The Employer Partnership Lead is the critical link between our schools and the DHL UK Foundation. Encompassing resource development, event planning and partnership working, this is a great opportunity to make a difference to young people's futures. This role will report into Ryan Gibson who joined the Trust in 2019 as National System Leader. He's an accomplished leader in the sector who was recently seconded as Senior Adviser for Careers at the Gatsby Foundation, where he led the national review of the Gatsby Benchmarks and the Foundation's work on the 'Next Ten Years of Good Career Guidance. Ryan will support you in managing Lift Schools' operational relationship with the DHL UK Foundation. You will be responsible for developing resources and workshops and for briefing employers to deliver crucial employability skills to hundreds of students in KS3, KS4 and KS5. Supported by you, DHL employees will lead classroom-based activities at selected schools and you will work with the DHL UK Foundation to plan a wide range of activities, including site visits and virtual encounters to help young people better understand and experience the world of work. You will be responsible for managing all aspects of this project, from design and implementation through to successful delivery, impact evaluation and reporting. As well as engaging schools across our network, this project will require integrated work across our central team and you will set out, and enact, a clear project management strategy to achieve this. What you'll need to succeed You will understand the flexibility this role requires, during delivery periods you will be on-site in our schools and at home the remainder and school holidays (it's worth noting we will pay for your travel). You will have relevant experience of working with young people either in an educational environment or a workplace situation alongside a proven track record of building relationships with a range of different stakeholders. Due to a maternity leave we are recruiting for an exciting part-time opportunity to lead on an innovative project between one of the largest MATs in the country and DHL UK Foundation. Please note, due to this being a maternity leave we will be reviewing applications as we receive them so we encourage you to apply ASAP. If you would like a confidential discussion or have any questions ahead of applying we'd love to hear from you. Please contact the recruitment manager, Jessica Billows. Who is Lift Schools? Lift Schools is made up of 62 primary, secondary and special schools, educating more than 35,000 pupils across the country. We believe education can transform lives - and we want every child in our schools to achieve their full potential. How we will support you We want you to feel supported, valued and able to grow throughout your career with Lift Schools. From high-quality professional development and career progression to wellbeing support and opportunities to connect and collaborate across our network, we invest in you so you can do your best work.

allJobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
allJobs.description: Salary: £67,890 - £73,299 per annum Grade: MAT6, SCP52-SCP56 Hours: 37 hours per week, all year round. Part-time applications will be considered. Location: Trust Central Office, Blackgates Primary Academy, with travel across Trust sites as required. Shape the financial future of Leodis Academies Trust Leodis Academies Trust is seeking an experienced, ambitious and strategically focused Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to join our senior leadership team. This is a key leadership appointment with responsibility for the strategic stewardship of the Trust’s finances, ensuring strong financial governance, sustainability, probity and compliance. Working closely with the CEO Principal, COO, Trustees and senior leaders, you will help ensure that our financial strategy and resources support the Trust’s ambitions and deliver the best possible outcomes for our schools and pupils. As CFO, you will lead the Trust’s finance function and central finance team, providing high-quality financial advice, challenge and assurance across the organisation. You will play an active role in Trust-wide strategy and attend Trustee meetings to report on financial matters. The role You will lead the Trust’s financial strategy, ensuring long-term sustainability, strong financial governance and regulatory compliance. Providing expert advice and assurance to Trustees and senior leaders, you will oversee financial operations, planning, budgeting, risk, audit, treasury, systems and value for money, while leading and developing a high-performing central finance team and building effective relationships with external partners. You will also work closely with Principals, School Business Managers and Office Managers, providing professional challenge and support around budgets and financial decision-making. About you We are looking for a fully qualified accountant with current membership of a relevant professional body, such as CIPFA, ICAEW, ACCA or CIMA, with significant post-qualification experience in a senior financial leadership role. Whilst you may not have held the post of CFO previously, you will bring substantial experience of leading financial strategy, managing significant financial resources, financial planning and modelling, financial risk and assurance, and leading and developing a finance team. Experience within education, particularly within a Multi-Academy Trust, and knowledge of academy funding arrangements would be an advantage, but not essential. Just as importantly, you will be a confident and credible leader who can make complex financial information accessible to different audiences. You will combine strong business acumen with excellent communication, leadership and influencing skills and have the confidence to provide both support and constructive challenge. You will demonstrate high standards of integrity and professional conduct, together with the resilience, adaptability, accuracy and attention to detail required for a senior Trust leadership role. Why Leodis? Leodis Academies Trust comprises Blackgates Primary Academy, East Ardsley Primary Academy, Hill Top Primary Academy, Westerton Primary Academy and Woodkirk Academy. As a Senior Executive Leader, you will work closely with the CEO Principal, COO, Trustees and academy leaders in a structure that gives the CFO a clear strategic financial leadership role, while benefiting from established operational leadership across the Trust. If you are a forward-thinking finance leader who can balance strategic ambition with sound financial stewardship, constructive challenge with collaboration, and strong governance with continuous improvement, we would be delighted to hear from you. Safeguarding Leodis Academies Trust is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff to share this commitment.
